narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The ratio is four to six, so my neck is four sixths of my height.
<bookmark mark='why'/>For eigh height of one hundred fifty centimetres, that is one hundred centimetres of neck!
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Six is the rest of the body, not the whole, so that slip is wrong.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 4/6 × 150 = 100 cm of neck; a child outline with a very long neck appears; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>To check, the neck and the rest must add up to your whole height.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Sixty and ninety make one hundred fifty, and sixty to ninety is four to six.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the crane; two check lines appear: neck + rest = height; 60 + 90 = 150 and 60 : 90 = 4 : 6

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu reads four to six and says his neck is four sixths of my height. Six is only the rest of the body, not the whole, so the bubble is struck.
